data.long_meaning: The name Revaan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ravana', which means 'mighty' or 'powerful'. In Hindu mythology, Ravana is known as the king of Lanka and the demon king who abducted Sita, the wife of Lord Rama. Despite his negative portrayal in the epic Ramayana, he is also revered as a powerful and intelligent figure.

data.cultural_impact: The name Revaan, derived from Ravana, brings to mind the strong and powerful being that Ravana was in Hindu mythology. It may evoke a sense of strength and resilience, as well as a reminder of the complexities and nuances of Hindu mythology where even powerful and supposedly 'evil' figures can be revered and remembered.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Revaan may be spiritually significant for those who believe in the power and complexity of the Hindu mythological figures. It may remind us of the potential for strength and power within ourselves, as well as a reminder of the importance of understanding the nuances and complexities of various spiritual beliefs. In a deeper sense, it can inspire us to embrace our own 'inner Ravana' and harness our personal power to overcome challenges and lead meaningful lives.

historical_references.reference: Revaan is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a king of the Vidarbha region in central India. He is a friend and ally of the Pandava brothers, and plays an important role in helping them gain victory in the Kurukshetra war.

historical_references.reference: In Jain texts, Revaan is described as a legendary leader of the Digambaras, a sect of Jainism. He is said to have lived during the 11th or 12th century CE and is revered for his spiritual achievements and his role in the spread of Jainism.
